text:
Morgan: quick note — during the 2am spike we had a messy handoff and customers saw 502s for ~12m. paging worked but context was fragmented. I want to propose a small automation + dashboard workstream to make capture + followup less noisy and faster. thoughts?

Alex: +1. Biggest pain was collecting customer impact details while still triaging. we ended up with a vague PM note and lost the exact affected endpoints.

Priya: agreed. also the on-call who picked up after the pager didn't get the post-incident summary — the handoff message was 'taking over' and nothing else. we should standardize the handoff payload.

Samir: idea: incident-bot could require a short structured capture at the moment the incident is created and again at handoff: affected_services, observed_customer_error_rate, visible_customer_impacts. store that in the incident record so the postmortem generator has fields to use.

incident-bot: @Morgan created incident INC-2026-1457: high-502-rate on inference-router. Severity: Sev2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-1457 :rotating_light:

Morgan: exact proposal sketch — three parts:
1) on-creation capture: when a pager triggers /incident create or incident-bot auto-creates, require minimal structured fields (dropdowns/short text).
2) handoff form: when someone uses "@oncall-bot take" or reacts :hand:, the bot prompts the outgoing oncall to paste key context (what they tried, hypothesis, mitigation in-flight, customer-facing symptoms).
3) ActionBoard dashboard: a compact widget that shows open remediation action items from recent incidents with owner, due-date, impact metric, and link to the incident + postmortem draft.

Alex: can we keep the creation form minimal? forced short answers are better. example fields: affected_customers (free text), endpoints_affected (csv), customer_visible (yes/no), estimated % requests failing (numeric), workaround_in_place (short).

Priya: +1 to minimal. also add a checkbox: schedule_postmortem_meeting (yes/no) — default to yes for Sev1/2. If yes, bot auto-suggests times based on oncall + PM calendars.

Samir: here's a very small prototype payload for the incident record (for UI and for the postmortem template):

```
incident_capture: {
  "affected_customers": "enterprise-a, sandbox users",
  "endpoints_affected": "/v1/generate,/v1/chat",
  "visible_symptom": "502s, increased latency",
  "estimated_error_rate_pct": "12",
  "workaround": "fallback to small-model pool",
  "schedule_postmortem": "true"
}
```

Priya: love it. for the handoff prompt, propose a tiny checklist the outgoing oncall must complete before transfer: hypothesis, mitigations applied, next steps, known customer tickets. it can be 4 short bullets.

Morgan: UX note — the bot should surface these fields in the incident timeline and include a one-click 'create postmortem draft' which pre-fills the template with those captured fields. keeps postmortem writing low-friction.

Alex: ActionBoard — what columns? I propose: Incident, Action, Owner, Due, Severity, Impact_metric, Status, Link. And allow quick filter by owner/team and sort by due date. Ideally ability to bulk remind owners.

Samir: backend: actions should be created as first-class objects in our action-tracker service with a link back to incident id. the dashboard just reads that. reminder cadence could be 3/7/14 days or custom.

Priya: automation for scheduling: if schedule_postmortem true, bot queries calendars of incident owner + PM + oncall and suggests 3 slots within 3 business days. user picks and bot creates event with agenda link (postmortem draft). saves event id to incident.

Morgan: minimal MVP scope for this sprint (2 weeks):
- incident-bot: required creation fields + store w/ incident record (Samir)
- oncall-bot: simple handoff prompt with 4 bullets (Priya)
- postmortem generator: one-click draft from incident fields (Alex)
- ActionBoard: basic widget that lists actions (read-only) and links to action-tracker (Morgan)

Priya: volunteer to own the handoff UX and copy for prompts. Samir owns incident-bot changes. Alex owns postmortem generator. Morgan will wire up dashboard and action-tracker integration.

incident-bot: created task: INC-2026-1457 -> PM: @Priya assigned, Owner: Samir for bot work, due: 2026-03-22 :white_check_mark:

Alex: tiny compliance question — storing customer identifiers in incident record: we should mark that field sensitive and encrypt at rest, accessible to oncall + CS + legal. I'll add a short policy note to the PR.

Samir: noted. encryption + RBAC for incident fields. will add to implementation checklist.

Morgan: sample action items from this thread to capture now:
- A1: implement creation capture on incident-bot (Samir) — due 2026-03-22
- A2: add handoff prompt and checklist to oncall-bot (Priya) — due 2026-03-22
- A3: postmortem one-click draft generator (Alex) — due 2026-03-24
- A4: ActionBoard widget MVP + link to action-tracker (Morgan) — due 2026-03-29
- A5: add encryption/RBAC for sensitive fields (Alex & Samir) — due 2026-03-26

Priya: I'll create the kickoff doc and add a few example incident capture UI mockups. putting a quick calendar for a 30m sync tomorrow 10:30 PT.

Samir: i'll open the incident-bot PR and tag the security folks for the encryption bits.

Morgan: one more ask — can we have the postmortem template include a small section called 'Customer-facing summary' auto-filled from the capture so PMs can copy into support comms? that was a pain this morning.

Alex: yes, will include a 2-3 sentence auto-summary generated from the fields. will show it prominently at top of draft.

SRE Dashboard: new ActionBoard widget created: https://sreboard.redwood/widgets/actionboard?view=inc_recent (MVP - read-only). share feedback here.

Morgan: thanks everyone. status: green to proceed. next: Priya will create kickoff doc + invite; Samir/ Alex/ Morgan split implementation work. we'll reconvene in three days for a quick sync and demo. :rocket:

Alex: thanks. tagging @eng-security for the encryption/RBAC review.

Priya: done — calendar invite sent.

Samir: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/incident-bot/pulls/82 — includes schema for new capture fields.

Morgan: closing thread with action items recorded above. please update action-tracker items as you make progress.

-- end of thread --
